transcript.content: Hello, it’s nice to meet you. What brings you in today?

Nice to meet you too. I came in because... well, I honestly can't see my studio, or really my life in general, getting back on track anymore. It just feels like no matter how hard I work, or what kind of payment plan they put in front of me... it's not going to make a difference. I just don't see a way out of it.
Do you feel down even when you aren’t thinking about your studio or finances?

Yeah, it's not just the money. Honestly, most days I wake up and... there's just this heavy, gray feeling already sitting on me before I even get out of bed. Even when I'm in the shop, you know, surrounded by the wood I used to love working with... it all just feels flat. I really have to fight with myself not to just stand there staring at nothing. It's just there all the time.
How long has this heavy, gray feeling been present?
Well, it's been going on since I took on the mortgage for the studio. That was a little over two years ago... I'd say about two years and two months now.
During these past two years, has there been a period of at least two months when you felt mostly like yourself and the heavy, gray feeling was gone?

No, I haven't had anything like that. I mean... maybe a day or two here and there where it wasn't quite as bad, but definitely not two whole months. It's pretty much been a constant thing this entire time.
Do you feel tired or low in energy most days?

Yeah, I do. It's... it's pretty bad, honestly. Even if I've been in bed all night, I just feel completely wiped out. By midmorning, my arms feel like I've been hauling heavy lumber all day, even if I haven't done much. Just doing the basics, like measuring or cutting, or even just trying to return a few phone calls... I can barely push through it. It takes everything I've got just to keep moving.
{"intent":"Assess for a change in sleep as an additional depressive symptom","question":"Since this began, have you noticed any change in your sleep?""}

Not really. I mean... I still sleep about the same amount I always have. I'm in bed for a normal amount of time. It's just that, like I said, it doesn't feel like it actually does any good. But as far as how much I'm sleeping or anything like that... no, I haven't noticed a change there.
{"intent":"Assess for difficulty concentrating as an additional depressive symptom","question":"Since this began, have you had trouble concentrating?""}

No, not really. I mean, my focus is about the same as it usually is. I can still measure things out and follow a plan for work. I don't get distracted or anything like that. I'm just tired while I do it, you know? But my concentration itself seems fine.
Since this began, have you noticed any change in your appetite?

No, my appetite's been pretty normal. I still eat about the same amount I always have. I mean, I haven't really noticed being more hungry or less hungry or anything like that. Just eating my regular meals, really.

final_diagnosis.reason: Persistent depressive disorder is supported by depressed mood and loss of interest or pleasure occurring most days for over two years without a symptom-free period of two months, accompanied by low energy and hopelessness. Functional impairment is present. A major depressive episode and adjustment disorder with depressed mood were considered, but the interview did not establish sufficient additional major depressive symptoms or a time-limited stress-response pattern.

confirmed_symptoms: Reports a heavy, gray feeling most days, present upon waking and persistent throughout the day.
Previously enjoyable woodworking and being in the studio now feel flat and emotionally unrewarding.
Markedly reduced energy and persistent fatigue despite normal sleep.
Pervasive hopelessness about the future and inability to see a way out of the financial and life situation.

additional_requirements: Chronicity exceeding two years was confirmed.

At least two associated depressive symptoms were confirmed: low energy and hopelessness.
Sleep, appetite, and concentration changes were explicitly denied.
